s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hyperpigmented skin lesion with irregular borders and satellite lesions, asymptomatic, with areas of regression
salient_findings: Irregular brown-black patch on the left lateral ankle
Confluent mottled black and brown macules with satellite lesions
Areas of regression noted at age 12
key_facts: Dermoscopy findings: discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas
Histopathology at age 9: compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction
Histopathology at age 12: atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
No induration palpated except at the previous biopsy site

differentials: Melanocytic Tumor of Uncertain Malignant Potential
per_call: Melanocytic Tumor of Uncertain Malignant Potential

shortlist.label: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical description of a progressive hyperpigmented skin lesion with irregular borders and satellite lesions

shortlist.label: Atypical Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: supported by histopathology findings of atypical compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction

shortlist.label: Dysplastic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to presence of random atypia and broad areas of regressive fibrosis in histopathology

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: cannot be entirely ruled out despite low gene expression testing score, given the lesion's progressive growth and atypical features

shortlist.label: Nevus of Ota
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of a hyperpigmented patch with blue and gray areas on dermoscopy, although less likely given the lesion's location and progression

raw.rationale: The large size of the lesion at onset, its slow but progressive growth, and the presence of satellite lesions are characteristic of congenital melanocytic nevi. The histopathology findings of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with the gene expression testing score consistent with a benign nevus, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Atypical Nevus
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows atypical features, the overall clinical and histological picture is more consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus.

rejected.label: Dysplastic Nevus
rejected.why: Dysplastic nevi are typically smaller and have different histological features than those described in this case.

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: The gene expression testing score and the lack of induration or other suspicious features make melanoma less likely.

rejected.label: Nevus of Ota
rejected.why: Nevus of Ota typically presents with blue-gray pigmentation in the distribution of the ophthalmic and maxillary branches of the trigeminal nerve, which does not match the description of this case.
